presetTallIn: More equations than unknowns, b in Col(A)
presetTallOut: More equations than unknowns, b outside Col(A)
nulGeom0: Nul(A) is a point: it only contains the zero vector.
nulGeom1: Nul(A) is a line through the origin.
nulGeom2: Nul(A) is a plane through the origin.
nulGeomN: Nul(A) is a subspace of dimension {k} through the origin.
caseRightSol: Infinitely many solutions: X = Rb + Nul(A).
caseLeftSol: It can only be X = Lb, and it works if b is in Col(A).
caseNoneSol: There is no formula with pseudoinverses.
pseudoBoth: A is square and rank(A) = n, so it has an inverse: A⁻¹A = AA⁻¹ = I.
pseudoRight: It exists because rank(A) = m: AR = I.
pseudoLeft: It exists because rank(A) = n: LA = I.
pseudoNone: rank(A) is less than m and less than n: neither the right inverse nor the left inverse exists.
noneConsistent: Even so, the system has a solution, but it has to be solved with Gaussian elimination.
noneInconsistent: Besides, the system has no solution: b is not in Col(A).
nullHint: Every vector v satisfies Av = 0. Adding a multiple of it to a solution gives another solution.
nullZero: Nul(A) = {0}: the only solution of AX = 0 is X = 0, so the solution of AX = b, if there is one, is unique.
particularHint: One specific solution of AX = b, the one you get by multiplying the inverse by b.
leftCandidate: If the system has a solution, it has to be X = Lb.
chosenHint: Move the sliders: X = Xp + Xh, with Xh in Nul(A).
checkOk: A·X equals b: it is a solution.
checkBad: A·X does not equal b: it is not a solution.
leftIn: b is in Col(A): X = Lb is the only solution.
leftOut: b is not in Col(A): the system has no solution, which is why X = Lb does not satisfy AX = b.
